_meta.notes: Consolidated, de-duplicated rule set for the Placed Cover Letter Writer. Each rule cites the research rule ids it came from (file:rule-id). Severities: block = must not ship; high = fix before ship; med = warn; low = style. check: regex|count|length (deterministic), llm (judge pass), flow (pipeline/UX), policy (product decision). Lexicon regexes are case-insensitive, multiline. Thresholds are uncalibrated (05 §6): calibrate on real student letters and aim for < 10% false positives on human letters.
_meta.auditFixes: 2026-10-18 audit 09: Overall/Ultimately soft (#5); negative parallelism needs a reframe (#5); Yahoo! exempt (#5); money only with intent words, med (#5); 'before deciding' dropped (#5); US-spelling soft pattern removed ('program' is British for software) (#5); realm/beacon/symphony/indelible soft (#6); Dear Sir/Madam low (#18); iStart 0.5 (#20); field fill 60% low (#21); full letter 220-380, hard 420 (#22); phrase-level triplet (#24); en/em/-- dashes counted together, high not block (#25); AI-policy regex moved to lib/employer-policy (#1). Rules with no code are marked implemented:false (#9).

skip.note: No letter accepted or no specific hook for an optional upload; produce 'why us' interview notes instead.

rules.rule: Choose the output mode (skip/full_letter/short_letter/field_answer/short_note/email/speculative) from the form and posting before drafting; never paste a full letter into a question box.
Never exceed a stated word/character limit; field answers fill 85–100% of it. Count characters including spaces and newlines when the limit is in characters.
Full letter body 250–400 words (hard max 450), 4–5 paragraphs, each ≤ ~110 words, one A4 page.
Field answers and short notes carry no letter furniture: no address, date, 'Dear…' or 'Yours…'. A field answer's first sentence answers the question using its key nouns.
Don't write a letter just because an optional upload exists: require at least one specific firm hook and one proof point the CV can't show, otherwise suggest skipping it.
Never offer a 'generic' (untailored) mode.
Every claim about the candidate traces to an evidence-pack item (a CV line ID, a profile field, or a user answer).
No number appears unless it appears in the sources.
Never invent a motivation, anecdote, contact, event attended or product usage; if none is given, write a factual role-fit sentence and flag it 'add your own reason'.
Firm facts (deal, result, programme feature, product) come only from the job description or user notes, each with a source; anything older than 12 months is flagged.

Mention visa status, right to work, disability, grades or gaps only if they are stored in the profile and the user opts in. Visa: ≤ 2 sentences in the final paragraph, with the duration taken from dated config. If the form has a right-to-work field, answer it there instead.
Name a third party (a person met) only after the user confirms.
If the job description or employer forbids AI use, switch to feedback-only mode (critique the user's own draft; generate no text) and warn the user.
Never compute or display an AI-detector score.
Never auto-submit; show the final text, the limit and how much of it is used before the user submits.
Name the exact company and role title (plus division/office, and the reference if one is given) in the first paragraph, or in the first sentence of a field answer.
No other employer's name (except past employers in the CV) and no placeholders.
Address 2–3 requirements from the job description, each with its own example.
Each 'why this firm' sentence must fail the swap test against the firm's top-3 rivals.
Connect each firm fact to the candidate's own experience or goal; no firm fact stands alone.
Put the candidate's own touchpoints (spring week, event, contact) first in 'why us' when they exist.
Use at most one company value, illustrated by one behaviour from the CV; never paraphrase the values page.
No run of 8 or more words copied from the job description or careers page (except the role title).
Raw website facts (headcount, offices, founding year, AUM) only when tied to the role in the same sentence.
Every trait claim (analytical, team player…) is followed by a concrete example in the same or the next sentence, or removed.
At least one concrete detail per body paragraph (a number, named project, tool, module, organisation or date).
Don't restate the CV: each example adds how/why/what changed; ≤ ~60% of sentences may paraphrase CV bullets; never write 'my CV shows'.
Use first-person active verbs for the candidate's own contribution ('I built', not 'we were involved in'); state the outcome when the source has one.
End each example with a 'so what' link to the target role.
Never open with a deficit ('Although I have no experience…').
Focus on what the candidate would contribute, not gain: 'opportunity to learn/develop/grow' at most once.
Societies and extracurriculars: at most 2, each with scale or outcome.
Tech/product/data roles: 1–2 proof links the user owns, placed next to the claim they support (max 3).
Put the stronger section first: 'why me' with direct experience, 'why them' with thin experience but strong research.
The opening sentence names the role and carries a specific hook; no throat-clearing opener.
The close gives a one-sentence fit summary plus a forward ask (interview, availability) in 25–50 words, with no stock filler.

Salutation: a named person ('Dear Ms Patel', no full stop) → else '{Firm} Graduate Recruitment Team' if the programme has one → else 'Dear Hiring Manager'. Never 'To whom it may concern' or 'Dear Sir/Madam'.
Sign-off: named → 'Yours sincerely'; unnamed → 'Yours faithfully' (configurable); email/short note → 'Kind regards' or first name. Fail on named + faithfully or on a bare US 'Sincerely,'.
Startup notes end with exactly one low-friction ask.
Zero hard-lexicon hits.
At most 3 distinct soft-lexicon hits per 300 words; fix by rewriting the sentence, not by swapping synonyms.
Keep user-supplied sentences verbatim (spelling and grammar fixes only) as locked spans.
Sentence rhythm: standard deviation ≥ 4 words, at least one sentence ≤ 8 words, mean ≤ 22, max 40.
Paragraph lengths vary (coefficient of variation ≥ 0.15 when there are 4 or more paragraphs).
≤ 35% of sentences start with 'I'; no two consecutive paragraphs start with 'I'; no 'I want'/'I like' in the opening.
Match the user's voice stats (contraction rate, first-person rate, sentence length) when a sample exists.
No more than 40% verbatim sentence overlap with the user's other letters.
Moderate self-promotion: ≤ 2 unsupported superlatives; never 'perfect/ideal candidate'; ≤ 1 evaluative adjective about the firm per paragraph.
en-GB spelling throughout; zero spelling or grammar errors.
UK date format, e.g. '17 October 2026'.
Prose only: no markdown, bullets, headings, emoji or exclamation marks.
Export both a PDF named First-Last_Cover-Letter_Company_YYYY-MM.pdf and a plain-text copy.
Use 3 or more key terms from the job description naturally; never keyword-stuff.
Consulting: never frame consulting as a stepping stone.
Never give salary, bonus, perks, prestige or exit opportunities as the motivation.
S&T: name the desk family and show engagement with markets.
Big 4: show realism about the qualification and the service line; 'why this Big 4' must not apply to the other three.
Asset management: state a buy-side motivation and the firm's investment style.
Actuarial: mention IFoA exam progress and the line of business when present.
PM: one user-level product observation, taken only from the user's notes; otherwise ask the user for one.
Data: each story runs question → method → decision.
Quant 'additional info' boxes: factual, ≤ 150 words, covering only why this firm, how you heard, and your timeline.
If the user flags a gap, weak grades or a reapplication, address it in one neutral sentence after the main evidence.

hard.pattern: \b(I hereby apply|I hope this (email|letter|message) finds you well|my name is)\b
hard.label: Cliché opener

hard.pattern: \b(team player|self[- ]starter|go[- ]getter|think outside the box|hit the ground running|fast learner|give 100%)\b
hard.label: Cliché

hard.pattern: \bI (look forward|would welcome the opportunity) to (discuss|discussing) how my (skills|experience)\b
hard.label: Formulaic close

hard.pattern: (as an AI|I hope this (letter|draft) helps|here is (a|your) (draft|cover letter)|certainly!)
hard.label: Chatbot leakage

hard.pattern: \b(a few years (in|at) consulting|exit opportunit(y|ies)|keep(ing)? my options open|stepping[- ]stone)\b
hard.label: Consulting stepping-stone

soft.pattern: \b(please do not hesitate to contact|at your earliest convenience|I hope to hear from you soon)\b
